title: An explicit 94-vertex cubic-residue candidate and certificate reduction
exact_target: Find a graph on at most 99 vertices with no four-clique that forces a monochromatic triangle in every two-coloring of its edges.
definition_tex:
\subsection{Definitions and mathematical statement}
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite simple undirected graph. It is $K_4$-free
if no four distinct vertices have all six possible edges between them.
Write $G\to(K_3,K_3)$ if for every map $c:E\to\{\mathrm{red},\mathrm{blue}\}$
there are distinct vertices $u,v,w$ whose three pairwise edges belong
to $E$ and receive the same color. Such a coloring is an edge coloring;
there is no proper-coloring requirement.
A graph satisfying both properties is an edge Folkman graph for
triangles with forbidden clique $K_4$.

The workshop challenge is to construct such a graph on fewer than
$100$ vertices. Equivalently, if
\[
 F_e(3,3;4)=\min\{|V(G)|:G\text{ is }K_4\text{-free and }
                                     G\to(K_3,K_3)\},
\]
the proposed target is $F_e(3,3;4)\le99$.
A complete construction must specify all vertices and edges and verify
both requirements. Verifying the absence of $K_4$ alone is insufficient:
the Ramsey condition quantifies over every two-coloring of the edges.
Conversely, a graph with the Ramsey property but containing a $K_4$
does not qualify. Vertices or edges removed from a larger candidate
must be accounted for in the verification, since deleting them may
destroy the Ramsey property. If the numerical target is impossible,
a proof that every graph on at most $99$ vertices fails at least one
condition would decide the challenge negatively.

\subsection{Short English statement}
Find a graph on at most 99 vertices with no four-clique that forces a monochromatic triangle in every two-coloring of its edges.
